strings.title: One Last Broadcast
strings.hint: Listen to the cassette's background noise. Where exactly can that hum be heard? Who was the only person to move around during the break?
strings.solvedText:
The killer: Nasser Al-Zahrani — the sound engineer.

Three years earlier, Ahmed stole Nasser's Night Podcast concept and turned it into Night Line, the show that made him famous. Nasser remained behind the control-room glass, adjusting the voice of the man who had stolen his life. He recorded the threat in that same room; its distinctive air-conditioning hum exposed him. He disabled the corridor camera, stole digoxin from guest Dr. Areej's bag to frame her, then put the dose in the cup while carrying the tray as he did every night.

The evidence against him: the inside-out glove in the control-room bin, the 96% cassette-noise match, his movements during the break, and his deleted messages: 'He will pay for what he stole.'
strings.summary.text: In the fifty-third minute of his late-night show Night Line, presenter Ahmed Fares drank his usual coffee and collapsed live on air before thousands of listeners. The building is locked at night. Only four people entered the studio after nine: the producer, the guest, the sound engineer and the catering attendant. The poison is in the cup alone… and the killer is within these soundproof walls.
strings.summary.victim.name: Ahmed Ibrahim Fares
strings.summary.timeline[1].l: Break — the only movement outside the rooms
strings.scene.address: Al-Mada FM studios — Studio 2 and control room
strings.scene.intro: Double glazing separates the presenter from the soundproof control room. Coffee is prepared in the kitchen and left on a serving table near the control-room door, then taken inside with the break scripts. The corridor camera, the only witness to the table, has been covered with tape since 21:50.
strings.scene.photos[0].cap: Broadcast desk — marker 1 beside the overturned cup
strings.scene.photos[1].cap: Cup and scripts after the collapse
strings.scene.notes[0]: Digoxin is in the cup only — the coffee pot is uncontaminated
strings.scene.notes[1]: Inside-out latex glove in the control-room bin
strings.scene.notes[2]: A digoxin vial disappeared from the guest's medical bag
strings.scene.notes[3]: Door log: only one exit during the break, 22:39–22:44
strings.evidence[0].title: The coffee cup
strings.evidence[0].desc: A fatal dose of digoxin in this cup alone; the pot is uncontaminated. It was poisoned between the serving table and its arrival at the presenter's desk.
strings.evidence[1].title: The cassette tape
strings.evidence[1].desc: Mailed a week earlier. An electronically distorted voice says, 'The final broadcast is near.' A distinctive air-conditioning hum can be heard in the background.
strings.evidence[2].title: Studio access log
strings.evidence[2].desc: Only four people after nine. The sound engineer was the only person to move during the break: exit at 22:39, return at 22:44.
strings.evidence[3].title: The latex glove
strings.evidence[3].desc: Hastily turned inside out, with traces of the same substance inside. Size M rules out larger hands.
strings.evidence[4].title: The missing digoxin vial
strings.evidence[4].desc: Disappeared from Dr. Areej's medical bag an hour after her arrival. The bag remained in the guest room beside the control room. She voluntarily reported the loss.
strings.evidence[5].title: Tape over the camera
strings.evidence[5].desc: A piece of black tape has blocked the lens since 21:50, before the guest even arrived. No fingerprints were found.
strings.evidence[6].title: Night Podcast manuscript
strings.evidence[6].desc: A program proposal signed by Nasser Al-Zahrani three years earlier. Its structure and segments match the current Night Line format.
strings.suspects[0].name: Wael Al-Salem
strings.suspects[0].alibi: 'I was in the observation booth behind the director throughout the show. I never approached the serving table.'
strings.suspects[0].statement: Ahmed was both the station's star and its headache. He was negotiating with a rival station, and I was trying to keep him with a better contract. Losing him alive would have been easier to bear than all our disputes. I watched the coffee follow its usual route: Souad leaves it on the serving table, and Nasser carries it inside with the break scripts. That night, Nasser was the only one who held the tray.
strings.suspects[1].name: Dr. Areej Al-Shehri
strings.suspects[1].relation: The episode concerned a defamation case involving her
strings.suspects[1].alibi: 'I was on air beside the victim the whole time, in full view of everyone.'
strings.suspects[1].statement: I came to answer an unfair campaign Ahmed's program had led against my clinic. I accepted because the truth was on my side. I always carry digoxin for my patients. When I noticed the vial missing, I reported it immediately myself. If I were the killer, I would have kept quiet. Whoever searched my bag did it while it was in the guest room, right beside the control room.
strings.suspects[2].name: Nasser Al-Zahrani
strings.suspects[2].relation: Creator of the original program concept
strings.suspects[2].alibi: 'During the break, I went to the bathroom for five minutes, then returned to the console.'
strings.suspects[2].statement: Three years ago, I brought Ahmed the Night Podcast proposal. He rejected it, then launched it in his own name two months later and took all the glory. I stayed behind the glass adjusting his voice as he read my old segments every night. Yes, I hate him. Yes, I went out during the break. But hatred does not kill. I was the last to touch the tray because that has been my job for five years.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Faisal
strings.witnesses[0].statement: From the observation booth, I saw the tray take its usual route: Souad → serving table → Nasser → Ahmed's desk, with the break scripts. Nobody else approached it. Ahmed took his first sip minutes after we returned to air, then his voice began to change.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Souad
strings.witnesses[1].statement: I made the coffee at 22:30, as I do every night: one pot and two cups. I tasted from the same pot to check the sugar, and nothing happened to me. I left the tray on the serving table and went straight back to the kitchen.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Caller
strings.witnesses[2].statement: A few minutes before the broadcast, the phone line opened by mistake for a few seconds. I heard a muffled argument behind the microphone: a young man's angry voice saying, 'Your time is up… at my expense.' Then the line closed.
strings.witnesses[2].items[0].label: Recorded telephone statement
strings.witnesses[2].items[0].text: The listener identified the argument's time as 21:57 — described in the file as just seven minutes before the corridor camera was disabled.
strings.witnesses[3].name: Studio guard
strings.witnesses[3].statement: No stranger entered after nine. The guest handed me her medical bag at reception and asked for it to be put in the guest room. I noticed Nasser leave once during the break and return unusually quickly.
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Emergency call during the broadcast
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body:
Director Faisal called an ambulance at the moment of collapse.
The presenter was transported within 11 minutes and died before reaching the hospital.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic medicine
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Toxicology report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body:
A fatal dose of digoxin, reported as absorbed within minutes, dissolved in sweetened coffee that masked its bitterness.
The cup's concentration is roughly equivalent to an entire vial.
strings.folders[1].docs[1].title: Death report
strings.folders[1].docs[1].body:
Acute cardiac arrest consistent with digoxin poisoning.
No signs of violence or resistance. Death at 23:20.
strings.folders[2].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Cup examination
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body:
Victim's fingerprints and a glove-pressure mark on the handle.
No third set of fingerprints. Whoever added the substance wore gloves.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Glove analysis
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body:
Digoxin residue inside the fingers of the inside-out glove.
Size M. The folds indicate hurried, tense removal.
strings.folders[2].docs[2].title: Cassette examination
strings.folders[2].docs[2].body:
The voice was distorted using common editing software.
A distinctive, constant-frequency air-conditioning hum is audible in the background. Referred for comparison with locations in the building.
strings.folders[3].name: Records
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Studio access log
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body:
After nine: only the producer, guest, sound engineer and catering attendant.
The only movement during the break: Nasser, 22:39–22:44.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Corridor camera report
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body:
The lens was blocked with a piece of black tape at 21:50.
The last clear frame shows an empty corridor. The camera was covered from a blind spot.
strings.folders[3].docs[2].title: Night Podcast dispute archive
strings.folders[3].docs[2].body:
An old administrative complaint by Nasser Al-Zahrani accused Ahmed Fares of stealing a program proposal. It was closed three years earlier for lack of jurisdiction.
Night Line launched two months later.
strings.folders[4].name: Interviews
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: Wael Al-Salem interview
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body:
The director confirms he remained in the observation booth throughout the episode.
Disclosed details of the victim's negotiations with a rival station.
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Dr. Areej Al-Shehri interview
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body:
Voluntarily reported the missing vial before the poison was identified.
Internal cameras confirm she never left her broadcast seat between 22:00 and the collapse.
strings.folders[4].docs[2].title: Nasser Al-Zahrani interview
strings.folders[4].docs[2].body:
Denied touching the medical bag, then could not explain his bathroom route past the guest room.
Denied the pre-broadcast argument; the listener's statement contradicts him.
strings.folders[4].docs[3].title: Souad interview
strings.folders[4].docs[3].body:
Confirmed preparing the coffee and tasting from the pot without symptoms.
The kitchen camera records her movements after leaving the tray.
strings.folders[5].name: Court orders
strings.folders[5].docs[0].title: Control-room search warrant
strings.folders[5].docs[0].body: Authorization to search the control room and staff lockers. The glove was recovered from the bin.
strings.folders[5].docs[1].title: Staff phone extraction warrant
strings.folders[5].docs[1].body: Authorization to extract data from all four phones and recover deleted material.
strings.folders[6].name: Classified files
strings.folders[6].docs[0].title: Background-noise comparison report
strings.folders[6].docs[0].body:
The cassette's background hum matches the control-room air conditioner with 96% confidence.
The threat was recorded in the control room itself, by someone with nighttime access to its keys.
strings.folders[6].docs[1].title: Deleted messages
strings.folders[6].docs[1].body:
Messages to an unidentified recipient were recovered from Nasser's phone, dated two weeks earlier:
'He will pay for what he stole. The final broadcast is near — and everyone will hear it this time.'
The cassette uses exactly the same phrase.
strings.reports[0].title: Preliminary report
strings.reports[0].author: Lead investigator — Lt. Col. H. Al-Qahtani
strings.reports[0].body:
A closed circle of four people, with poison in the cup but not the pot.
Cup route: Souad → serving table → Nasser → presenter. Every step is documented except the five-minute break.
strings.reports[1].title: Toxicology laboratory report
strings.reports[1].author: Central forensic laboratory
strings.reports[1].body:
The dose equals an entire vial, most likely the guest's missing vial.
Whoever took it needed two minutes alone with the bag in the guest room.
strings.reports[2].title: Movement reconstruction report
strings.reports[2].author: Reconstruction team
strings.reports[2].body:
Break reconstruction: the route from the control room to the bathroom passes both the guest room and the serving table.
Five minutes is exactly enough to take the vial, prepare the cup and return.
strings.notes[0].text: Poison in the cup, not the pot — narrow the circle
strings.notes[1].text: Who knew Ahmed always took his first sip just after the break?
strings.notes[2].text: The cassette came from inside, not outside
